prize_parts.citation: For developing the political-economy theory of trade policy, showing how organised interests shape the structure of protection.

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged after round 1: a single part on B001 for Helpman and Grossman, with a narrow citation. The case rests on three things I weigh the same way for every field. First, the protection-for-sale framework turned lobbying and tariff formation into a tractable general-equilibrium model, and so made an old question about why policy departs from efficiency measurable. Second, the credit sits cleanly with two people who built the programme jointly, so no one needs to be arbitrarily excluded. Third, the core work is about thirty years old and has been extended, estimated, criticised and taught, so maturity is not in doubt. From an economic-history vantage, the question of who obtains protection and why is central to explaining long-run policy regimes, and this framework gives it a disciplined structure that historians and political scientists also use. The chair's question on citation scope has pushed me to a firmer view: confine the citation to the political economy of trade protection. The growth-and-trade strand is real joint work, but the ballot does not define it as the discovery, and any overlap with other prizes is something I cannot verify from the supplied evidence. I do not treat the number of colleagues preferring B001 as evidence of merit. The case stands on the framework's content, attribution and maturity.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is the empirical record. Support for the specific protection-for-sale predictions is mixed, and structural parameters are sensitive to specification and setting. Part of the contribution is therefore an organising framework and research programme, not a confirmed quantitative result, and a citation must not overclaim. A second reservation is distinctness: trade was recognised in 2008, and colleagues report that innovation-led growth was recognised in 2025. I have not verified the scope of either prize. A third is that Helpman's separate firm-heterogeneity work on B030 means the committee could choose to honour trade through that line. If the committee wants a prize resting on tested findings and design-based evidence, B018 is the stronger comparison and I do not dismiss it.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson prefers B018 for Autor, Dorn and Hanson. She moved from Katz to Dorn after the attribution objections and now words the citation around technology and trade shocks to labour demand, without claiming priority for the task framework. She treats the debate over shift-share identification and persistence as evidence of maturity.
responses.response: Her move to Dorn and her narrower wording answer the two objections I raised in round 1: mixing the skill-premium strand with the China-shock strand, and leaving out someone central to the core papers. B018 is now a more defensible configuration than it was, and it is why I keep it as my first alternative. I still read the evidence differently on timing. A decade of replication and re-estimation does show durability, but the size and persistence of the effects are still being revised, and the task-framework antecedents remain uncredited. A citation confined to the trade-shock evidence would be an empirical-design contribution with a debated long-run interpretation. I weigh that as less settled than a framework absorbed for three decades. This is a difference of weighting, not of importance, and I would support Autor, Dorn and Hanson if the committee moved there.

responses.point: Krusell prefers B002 for Pakes, Berry and Levinsohn but now calls B001 a close alternative. He finds the mixed empirical record of protection-for-sale more worrying than the B001 supporters do. He says the case for B002 is its validation by thirty years of practice, and he would not widen the B001 citation to growth.
responses.response: I agree with his refusal to widen the citation, and it supports my narrow wording. On empirical standing, I accept that BLP has been validated by use in merger review and antitrust in a way protection-for-sale has not. I would still distinguish two kinds of validation. A toolkit is validated when practitioners adopt it. A framework is validated when it makes a question testable and organises the evidence, including the failures. On that standard B001 qualifies, though less strongly than a confirmed result would. For B002 the credit problem remains: Bresnahan and Reiss fall outside the three-name cap, and Pakes's dynamic-games work is partly separate from the demand framework. I would not present that as a weakness of method over discovery. That is why B002 stays second among my alternatives, and why I would support it if the committee judged B001's empirical standing too thin.

responses.point: Dreber prefers B030 for Melitz and Helpman because firm heterogeneity and selection have faced denser empirical confrontation than protection-for-sale. She names the omission of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum as the main weakness and says the contribution centres on one landmark paper.
responses.response: I accept her empirical point: the firm-level framework has been confronted with micro data more densely, and that counts in its favour. I would not use it to settle the choice, because the attribution problem she names is the very thing a citation has to get right. The exporter facts and parallel models of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum cannot be placed inside a three-name set without weakening the Melitz-Helpman core. By her own account the contribution also rests heavily on a single 2003 paper. I agree with her that B001 and B030 credit distinct contributions by Helpman and are alternative framings, not additive ones. My answer to the chair's question on the rule is that the committee should judge each on its own content and attribution, and a Grossman-Helpman award would not preclude later recognition of the firm-level strand. If the committee were to favour B030, I would want the attribution question settled before the vote.

responses.point: Teorell prefers B001 but has a citation that names both organised interests in trade policy and the integration of innovation and growth into trade theory. He treats the growth strand as supporting, not co-equal, and keeps the framing question open.
responses.response: I share his view that the framing question is the most useful open issue. My conclusion differs on the citation. Even as a supporting strand, naming growth invites the overlap question with other prizes, which none of us has verified, and it makes the prize look like two awards merged into one. A narrow citation on trade protection lets the contribution stand on what the ballot defines as the discovery. It also keeps the argument about empirical standing honest, because a clause about growth cannot rescue a weakness in the protection-for-sale evidence. If the committee wants the broader wording, I would want someone to show what the growth strand adds to the case, not merely that it exists.

uncertainties: How much weight the mixed empirical record of protection-for-sale should carry against the framework's conceptual and agenda-setting contribution. This is the main open question and I hold my view with moderate confidence.

Whether the committee will see B001 as sufficiently distinct from the 2008 trade prize and the reported 2025 growth prize. I rely on colleagues' descriptions and have not verified either prize's scope.
How to handle Helpman's credit on both B001 and B030 if the committee splits on which trade line to honour.

Whether Autor, Dorn and Hanson is a stable three-name set for B018 now that Hjalmarsson has converged on it, and whether the persistence of the China-shock effects will hold up to continued re-estimation.
Whether the BLP triple in B002 can be defended without Bresnahan and Reiss.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile for B001, Helpman or Grossman. My profile lists Lund economic-history collaborators, Lund-linked colleagues and a cross-disciplinary tie with Johannes Lindvall. None of them is credited on B001 or on my alternatives B018 and B002. My profile documents no collaboration or institutional tie to any credited name on those ballots. I disclosed familiarity with the political-economy literature in my opening as relevant to B036 only. It does not bear on this proposal.
